Cc: security@atlasfinance.com
Date: 2025-07-03T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Atlas Security: request for vulnerability management evidence and SLA clarification

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Our security team is working through the vendor evidence pack for Q3 and we need the following from Redwood to close our SIG/SOC2 review: 

- A short attestation document that outlines your vulnerability scan cadence (authenticated vs unauthenticated), SCA/OS/third-party coverage, and the SLA for CVE remediation by severity.
- A copy of the most recent authenticated network and container scan summary (just the executive summary is fine).
- Any documented exception or compensating-control process you follow for private instances (we have a legacy connector that runs in our VPC).

Can you turn these around by EOD Friday? If that's tight, please propose a date and we'll escalate internally.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Information Security
Atlas Finance

If Friday is still the target, great — otherwise Monday morning is acceptable.

Elena

Subject: Re: Atlas Security: request for vulnerability management evidence and SLA clarification

Elena — attaching the attestation and a short statement of our remediation SLAs below. See attachment: vm-attestation-letter.pdf (signed by me).

--- attestation excerpt ---
Redwood Inference vulnerability management attestation (executive summary):
- Scan cadence: Authenticated internal/container scans: weekly; External network scans: weekly; Full SCA (software composition analysis): monthly; Ad-hoc scans triggered by CI alerts or new upstream advisories.
- Coverage: OS packages, container images, third-party libs (SCA), and host-based packages. We use a combination of authenticated Nessus-style scanning and agent-assisted image scanning for container registries.
- SLA (remediation target windows measured from vendor-detected CVE publication or internal discovery):
  * Critical (CVSS 9-10): Detect -> Triage within 24h; Remediation or approved compensating control within 30 days (accelerated hotpatch when exploitable in production).
  * High (CVSS 7-8.9): Triage within 72h; Remediation within 60 days.
  * Medium (CVSS 4-6.9): Remediation within 120 days as part of scheduled patch waves.
  * Low (CVSS 0-3.9): Routine tracking and regular dependency updates.
- Exceptions: For private VPC connectors, we support a documented exception process—request, compensating controls evaluation, mitigating monitoring, and a time-boxed approval (maximum 90 days before re-evaluation). Template attached: patch-schedule.ics (calendar stub) and process link in Drive.

I will upload the signed PDF and redact any customer-sensitive rows in the scan summary. If you want a formal DocuSign signature for procurement, we can send that link (included below).

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vm-attestation-letter.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]
